AK-senate.statusNote: Final field for the November ranked choice general, certified Aug 31: Mary Peltola (D, 49.5%), Sen. Dan Sullivan (R, 41.4%) and Dan J. Sullivan of Petersburg (R, 2.5%) advanced from the Aug 18 top-four primary. David Leslie (D) finished fourth but withdrew Aug 31, so fifth-place finisher Gerald Heikes (R, 1.1%) takes the fourth ballot spot. Full researched entries added Sep 2, 2026 for the two candidates who were on the certified ballot with no positions on file: Gerald Heikes (repro scored, rest documented null) and Daniel J Sullivan of Petersburg (3 axes scored, rest documented null; not the incumbent senator).

AK-governor.statusNote: Open seat: Gov. Mike Dunleavy is term-limited and cannot seek a third consecutive term. In the Aug 18 top-four primary, Jonathan Kreiss-Tomkins (D), who represented Sitka and Southeast Alaska in the Legislature for a decade, and former Anchorage state Sen. Tom Begich (D) lead with about 22% and 20%. Conservative activist and business owner Bernadette Wilson (R) holds third at about 10%. The fourth spot is not settled: former Anchorage Mayor Dave Bronson (R) leads a tight pack, with certification expected Aug 31. The November general uses ranked choice voting. Certified fourth-spot correction, Sep 2 2026: Tom Begich (D), who finished second in the Aug 18 primary, officially withdrew Aug 31; the app's advancing list should have him REMOVED (fragment format cannot remove ids). That promoted Bernadette Wilson to second and Dave Bronson to third. The fourth slot was Treg Taylor's until Lt. Gov. Nancy Dahlstrom disqualified him Aug 31 for incomplete financial disclosures; his running mate Candice English took his spot on the ticket with Jodi Taylor (Treg's wife) as her new running mate. As of Sep 1, Alaska's News Source still described English's ticket status as pending compliance review of Jodi Taylor's disclosure, with a possible further shuffle to sixth- or seventh-place finishers if she is also disqualified. Certified final four for the November ranked-choice general as of Sep 2, 2026: Jonathan Kreiss-Tomkins (D, 22.5%), Bernadette Wilson (R, 10.1%), Dave Bronson (R, 8.1%), Candice English (R, pending).

senate.name: John W. Hickenlooper

sources.label: CPR: Hickenlooper defeats Gonzales in Democratic primary

senate.now: U.S. Senator from Colorado, seeking a second term; won the June 30, 2026 Democratic primary over state Sen. Julie Gonzales 57 to 43.
senate.background: Former Colorado governor (2011-2019) and Denver mayor; elected to the U.S. Senate in 2020. Focuses on energy, health care costs, and Colorado infrastructure funding.
priorities: Lowering health care and prescription drug costs

cost.label: Reintroduced bill extending Medicare's inflation rebate penalties to commercial insurance: "Our bill will deliver those same savings to Americans with private insurance" (Hickenlooper senate.gov)

health.label: Voted against the 2025 reconciliation bill over Medicaid/ACA cuts: warned of "17 million Americans losing health insurance by 2034" (Hickenlooper senate.gov)

housing.label: Championed the ROAD to Housing Act, which cuts federal building red tape while also restricting large investor purchases of single-family homes: "Let's build more homes... and ultimately lower the cost of housing" (Hickenlooper senate.gov)

immigration.label: Voted against the unamended Laken Riley Act, citing indefinite detention of children without due process (Hickenlooper senate.gov)

taxes.label: Opposed the 2025 reconciliation tax law as "lavish tax cuts for the wealthiest Americans" that would "increase our national debt by more than $3.3 TRILLION" (Hickenlooper senate.gov)

climate.label: Celebrated Senate passage of a major clean-energy investment package: "We'll reduce carbon emissions 40 percent by the end of the decade" (Hickenlooper senate.gov)

repro.label: Co-sponsored the Women's Health Protection Act to codify Roe v. Wade: "women have the freedom to make their own health choices" (Hickenlooper senate.gov)

democracy.label: Co-sponsored a bill to protect vote-by-mail, citing Colorado's 99.99% count accuracy: opposes the president's "attempts to rig the election and attack our right to vote" (Hickenlooper senate.gov)

at-large.name: Julie Fedorchak

sources.label: House roll call 114, 2025, California Clean Cars waiver disapproval

at-large.now: U.S. House of Representatives (North Dakota at-large)
at-large.background: Freshman U.S. Representative for North Dakota's at-large district since January 2025 and a member of the moderate Republican Governance Group. She spent twelve years on the North Dakota Public Service Commission, from 2013 to 2025, regulating utilities and pipelines, and campaigns on that record. She has introduced legislation to eliminate the Inflation Reduction Act's wind and solar tax credits for new projects, arguing intermittent generation poses reliability risks to the grid. She was renominated in the June 9, 2026 primary over Alex Balazs.
priorities: Unleash domestic energy and agriculture production
Cut federal spending and balance the budget

cost.label: Campaign priorities are to 'Curb Inflation That Is Crushing Families', 'Rein in Overreaching Federal Agencies', 'Stop out of Control Spending and Balance the Budget' and 'Unleash America's Energy and Agriculture Industries', with a record of 'Cutting Regulatory Red Tape' and 'Fighting Against Over-Regulation of the Coal Industry' (campaign site)

health.label: Calls the Affordable Care Act the 'Unaffordable Care Act' and says 'Obamacare is anything but affordable'; voted against the Democrat-led discharge petition to extend the enhanced premium tax credits; wants Medicaid 'reforms' that 'restore the program to its original mission'; health decisions belong with 'doctors and patients in North Dakota, not in Washington, D.C.' (House office issues page)

immigration.label: 'It was something I campaigned on. I would give us an A on our work so far. We have basically shut the border down' (North Dakota Monitor candidate issue spotlight)

taxes.label: Voted Aye on H.R. 1, titled 'One Big Beautiful Bill Act' on the roll call, on the motion to concur in the Senate amendment, July 3, 2025; it passed 218 to 214 (House roll call 190)

climate.label: Voted Yea on H.J.Res.88, titled on the roll call as congressional disapproval of the EPA rule on 'California State Motor Vehicle and Engine Pollution Control Standards; Advanced Clean Cars II; Waiver of Preemption', May 1, 2025; it passed 246 to 164 (House roll call 114)

repro.label: 'As a Christian, wife, and mother, I believe in the sanctity of life and am committed to protecting the unborn'; the page carries 'Fedorchak Votes to Pass Two Pro-Life Bills', January 23, 2026 (House office issues page)

safety.label: Voted Aye on H.R. 6260, the Keeping Violent Offenders Off Our Streets Act, May 14, 2026, which passed 243 to 179 (House roll call 169)

OK-governor.statusNote: Open seat, Gov. Stitt is term-limited. Former state Sen. Mike Mazzei defeated Attorney General Gentner Drummond by 2,020 votes out of more than 371,000 cast in the Aug 25 Republican runoff; Drummond conceded. House Minority Leader Cyndi Munson won the Democratic nomination June 16. Independents Jerry Griffin, Robert Brooks and Orlando Lynn Bush are also on the November ballot. Independents Jerry Griffin, Robert Brooks and Orlando Lynn Bush are confirmed on the November general ballot per NonDoc's filing coverage and News9's general-election preview; no documented policy positions were found for any of the three after two search rounds each, so all three now carry full curated entries that are all-null with dated dead-end notes.

OK-senate.statusNote: Open seat: Sen. Markwayne Mullin resigned in March 2026 after his confirmation as Homeland Security secretary; appointed Sen. Alan Armstrong is not running. Rep. 14.background: Thurman Bill Bartie is a lifelong Port Arthur resident who served two terms as mayor beginning in 2019, leading the city through hurricanes, flooding and the COVID-19 pandemic. He holds a political science degree from Lamar University, a mortuary science certification, and a Master of Ministry from Tennessee Temple University Baptist Seminary. VT-house-at-large.statusNote: Rep. Becca Balint (D) seeks re-election against Army veteran Gerald Malloy (R). Independents Phoenix Altair, Adam Ortiz, Suzanne Seymour and Ryan Walton are also listed for the November ballot. Positions researched Aug 17, 2026. The two overlap on 7 of the 10 issues; cost of living, housing and voting rules are one-sided and carry no match weight for the candidate who lacks them. governor.name: Rebecca Bextel

sources.label: Cowboy State Daily: CheckGate's Rebecca Bextel Running For Governor With Wyoming Constitution Party
WyoFile: CheckGate's Rebecca Bextel launches 'insurance policy' bid for Wyoming governor
Oil City News: Republican Barlow advances to face Democrat Casner, Constitution Party's Bextel for Wyoming governor

governor.now: Teton County conservative activist and real estate business co-owner; Constitution Party nominee for governor
governor.background: Bextel is a Teton County activist originally from Alabama who lives in Jackson with her husband and four daughters and co-operates Mountain Business Center, a real-estate and registered-agent services firm. She was active in Republican Party politics as a precinct committeewoman, state committeewoman, and 2020/2024 RNC alternate delegate before an unsuccessful 2025 bid for state party chair and her resignation as Teton County GOP committeewoman. She drew statewide attention in the 2026 legislative session over 'Checkgate,' hand-delivering campaign checks to House members on the chamber floor; a House investigation found no bribery but admonished her conduct, and a criminal investigation remains open. She switched to the Constitution Party, saying it is 'not about abandoning conservative principles' but 'returning to them.'

housing.label: As a state legislator she championed House Bill 141, which 'sought to ban housing mitigation fees statewide' (it passed the House and died in the Senate) (Cowboy State Daily)

climate.label: Governor platform lists 'energy dominance' as a core plank (Cowboy State Daily)

education.label: Governor platform lists 'parental rights' as a core plank alongside limited government and pro-life values (Cowboy State Daily)

repro.label: Governor platform explicitly lists 'pro-life values' as a core plank (Cowboy State Daily)

taxes.label: Promises 'meaningful, permanent property-tax reform that protects homeowners,' limits on excessive assessment increases, and a responsible fuel-tax reduction (rebeccaforwyoming.com)

immigration.label: Would withdraw Wyoming from the federal refugee resettlement program, end policies letting illegal immigrants obtain Wyoming driver's licenses, and ensure Wyoming 'will never become a sanctuary state' (rebeccaforwyoming.com)

governor.name: Megan Degenfelder
governor.background: Wyoming Superintendent of Public Instruction since 2023; sixth-generation Wyomingite from Casper who spent nearly a decade in government affairs for coal, oil and gas companies and once staffed then-Rep. Cynthia Lummis. Cancer survivor and rugby coach. Endorsed by President Trump, who calls her 'MAGA Megan', and by Rep. Harriet Hageman.
priorities: Wyoming energy dominance and local control of lands

cost.label: 'The government doesn't create jobs, the private sector does': eliminate regulations, though data centers 'cannot build here if you will increase rates for residents' (WyoFile election guide)

taxes.label: Property tax relief and reducing nonessential spending while leveraging energy revenue to fund essential services (WyoFile election guide)

climate.label: Prioritizes Wyoming 'energy dominance', protecting grazing, energy and timber development; nearly a decade in coal, oil and gas regulatory affairs (WyoFile election guide)

education.label: Supported legislation authorizing charter schools and a voucher program for private tuition; as superintendent pushed a legislative agenda to cement school choice and expand parental control (Wikipedia)

repro.label: Opposes any exceptions to abortion bans: 'I can't accept any exception when it comes to life' (WyoFile)

WY-senate.statusNote: Open seat, Sen. Cynthia Lummis is retiring. Rep. Harriet Hageman (R) and former state Rep. James Byrd (D) won their Aug 18 primaries.

WY-governor.statusNote: Open seat, Gov. Mark Gordon is not seeking a third term. State Sen. Eric Barlow (R) defeated Megan Degenfelder in the Aug 18 primary. Kenneth Casner (D) won the Democratic nomination. Rebecca Bextel of Jackson (Constitution Party) is also on the November ballot. Positions researched and sourced for Rebecca Bextel (Constitution) as of Sep 2, 2026.

WY-house-at-large.statusNote: Secretary of State Chuck Gray (R) won a crowded nine-way August 18, 2026 Republican primary to succeed Harriet Hageman, who ran for Senate instead; Lisa Kinney won the Democratic primary; Constitution nominee Jeff Haggit, Libertarian nominee Shawn Johnson, and independent Daniel Workman also qualified for the November ballot (The Green Papers Wyoming 2026 general candidate roster; WyoFile).
